text: Because network nodes verify and validate chain transactions before execution under a distributed consensus model, recording a fraudulent transaction on the blockchain is extremely rare.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain Technology and Race in Corporate America (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3071378

isBasedOn.name: Blockchain Technology and Race in Corporate America

abstract: Blockchain's distributed consensus model, e.g., the network "nodes" verify and validate chain transactions before execution of the transactions, makes it extremely rare for a fraudulent transaction to be recorded in the blockchain.34
